body.p: This paper is submitted in response to the non-final Office Action mailed January 26, 2024. At that time, claims 21-36 were pending, and claims 1-20 were cancelled. In the Office Action, claims 27-29 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(b) as being anticipated by Ive et al. (US 2024/0012601; hereinafter "Ive"). Additionally, claims 21-26, 35, and 36 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as unpatentable over Ive in view of Saur et al. (US 2018/0308451; hereinafter "Saur") and further in view of Samec et al. (US 2016/0270656; hereinafter "Samec"). Furthermore, claim 30 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as unpatentable over Ive in view of Samec, and claims 31-33 were rejected as unpatentable over Ive in view of Saur.
By this paper, Applicant amends claims 21, 23, 25-28, and 35. No claims are presently cancelled or added.

All the pending claims were rejected under either 35 U.S.C. § 102 as anticipated by Ive or under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as unpatentable over Ive in view of Saur or Samec (or both). Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections.
The standard for a Section 102 rejection is set forth in M.P.E.P 706.02, which provides:
"... for anticipation under 35 U.S.C. 102, the reference must teach every aspect of the claimed invention either explicitly or impliedly. Any feature not directly taught
must be inherently present."

Additionally, M.P.E.P. § 2141 sets forth the Graham factual enquiries that should be considered when making an obviousness rejection under Section 103: 1) ascertaining the scope and content of the prior art; 2) ascertaining the differences between the claimed invention and the prior art; and 3) resolving the level of ordinary skill in the pertinent art. (Citing Graham v. John Deere, 383 U.S. 1, 148 USPQ 459 (1966).) In addition, M.P.E.P. §§ 2141 and 2142 set forth that
"the analysis supporting a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103 should be made explicit." (Citing KSR International Co. v. Teleflex Inc. (KSR), 550 U.S. 398, 82 USPQ2d 1385 (2007).)

For a rejection under Section 103 to stand, it must explicitly set forth 1) factual findings showing that each claim element was known in the art at the time of the invention, and 2) factual findings showing that one of ordinary skill in the art, at the time of the invention, would have found it obvious to modify or combine the teachings to arrive at the claimed invention. (See,for example, the enumerated required articulations set forth in M.P.E.P. § 2143 for each lettered rationale.)
All of the rejections rely on Ive. Accordingly, the independent claims are now amended to overcome the Ive reference, as explained in more detail below.

Independent claim 21 is amended to recite a therapeutic training device comprising: a head mounted display comprising: an outward facing video display comprising a transparency that is variable; and a light having an adjustable brightness to illuminate eyes of a wearer, wherein adjusting at least one of the transparency and the brightness allows an observer to see the eyes of the wearer through the outward facing video display.

Similarly, independent claim 27 recites a therapeutic training device, comprising: eyeglass frames; an outward facing video display positioned within the eyeglass frames; and a controller coupled to the outward facing video display to control a display of media content on the video display, such that the display of media content is viewable by a patient when the therapeutic training device is worn by a user, wherein the outward facing video display is see-through from the side of the user.

In both cases, the video display is see-through (e.g., so that an observer can directly see the user's eyes, or so that the user can see the surrounding world past the display). This differs substantially from Ive, in which the user can see only an inward-facing screen (which can display

the user's surroundings, but which is not see-through to allow the user to see their surroundings directly). Similarly, although an observer of the Ive device can, in some cases, see a representation of the user's eyes on an outward facing screen, the observer cannot see the user's actual eyes, because the display is not transparent. Indeed, if the Ive device were to lose power or malfunction, the wearer would need to remove the device in order to see their surroundings or to allow observers to see their eyes.

Furthermore, a person of ordinary skill in the art would not think to modify Ive to make it transparent (by combining it with other references or otherwise), thereby allowing an observer to see the user's actual eyes. Indeed, it does not appear that doing so would work, because making the outer display of Ive transparent would not allow an observer to see the user's eyes; rather, the observer would see a solid panel (e.g., the HMD housing) behind the display, circuitry elements, and/or the inward-facing screens configured to allow the user to perceive their surroundings. (See Ive paragraphs [0123]-[0126]). Indeed, Ive would require significant and substantial modification and restructuring in order to allow for an observer to see a wearer's actual eyes (and not a displayed representation thereof) or vice versa, such that it would not be obvious to the skilled artisan to do so (whether alone or in combination with any other references).

In light of the foregoing, it is Applicant's belief that the claim set as provided herein overcomes all rejections made by the Office in the Office Action. Thus, Applicant respectfully submits that for at least the reasons provided herein, the claim set as provided herein overcomes all rejections made by the Office in the Office Action.
Applicant also submits that the amendments to the claims are supported by the original disclosure as filed, as evidenced by at least paragraphs [0010] and [0113] of the specification.

In view of the foregoing, Applicant respectfully submits that all claims are now in condition for allowance. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that a Notice of Allowance be issued in this case. Please debit any additional fees, or credit any over payment, to Deposit Account No. 50-0843. If there are any remaining issues preventing allowance of the pending claims that could be clarified by telephone, the Examiner is requested to call the undersigned attorney.
